A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 22 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v4, including their appendices, are readable, and corresponding theorems, proofs, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports original simulations of training-conditional coverage on four UCI regression datasets.

after.justification: v4 retains the Figure 1 simulations and adds an oracle-versus-estimated-weight experiment on Concrete Compressive Strength in Figure 2.

M1.justification: v4 adds an estimated-weight variant: Section 4 defines normalized estimated likelihood ratios, and Figure 2 uses Gaussian kernel density estimation. v2 documents oracle likelihood-ratio weighting only. The underlying conformal set constructions remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wine Quality, Abalone, Concrete Compressive Strength, and Combined Cycle Power Plant for regression under exchangeability and covariate shift. Figure 2 reuses Concrete; the new self-supervised learning and adversarial discussions introduce no evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds a direct comparison between oracle weights and Gaussian-KDE estimated weights. Figure 1's ordinary-versus-weighted conformal comparison is retained; no additional named conformal baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: v2's Figure 1 caption states 1000 training samples. v4's Appendix E instead reports 525 for Wine, Abalone, and Power Plant, and 360 for Concrete. This changes the reported setting; the identical Figure 1 plots do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds a targeted robustness analysis of likelihood-ratio estimation on Concrete Compressive Strength. Figure 2 tests how replacing oracle weights with estimated weights affects coverage, beyond the retained illustration of dispersion under covariate shift.

E5.justification: Both versions report coverage histograms without repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 2 follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: The four Figure 1 plots are identical across versions. New Figure 2 reports substantially lower coverage with estimated weights than with oracle weights within the later version's experiment.

T1.justification: v4 adds an estimated-weight perturbation bound and expands the supporting probability proofs. Theorem 2 and Lemma 4 explicitly state absolute-continuity/finiteness assumptions and replace the test-distribution probability with the calibration-distribution probability in the effective sample size. Lemma 2 changes its 6CK coefficient to 4CK, and old Remark 2 is removed. Most principal bounds remain intact. Corollary 1 introduces an L2-norm definition missing a square root.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the suggestion that the bounds could produce more efficient prediction sets and instead emphasizes characterizing reliability through shift severity and training size. The central contribution of training-conditional PAC coverage bounds is retained.

C2.justification: v4 explains how likelihood-ratio estimation introduces an additional error term whose concentration depends on the estimator. It also discusses possible self-supervised learning applications and adversarial or label-noise research directions. The limitation that the stability assumptions are verified only for ridge regression remains.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds explicit training/calibration/test counts and dataset-specific exponential-tilt vectors, while Figure 2 identifies Gaussian KDE. However, v4 removes v2's explicit description of the simulation learner as Gaussian-kernel RKHS regression.

R1.justification: v4 adds six references supporting the new self-supervised learning and robustness discussion and removes Yukich (1985). The principal positioning against Liang and Barber and earlier weighted conformal work remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 removes the one-sentence unfinished section on fully conditional prediction, adds a conclusion, and introduces appendix subsections for background and experimental details. It also makes targeted prose and author-information edits. Most existing exposition and section progression remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into TMLR style, changing typography, text width, title and author arrangement, running headers, and equation placement. Figure 1 is resized and recaptioned while retaining its plots; Figure 2 adds a new two-distribution histogram.

improvement.justification: The estimated-weight analysis and Figure 2 make the practical consequences of likelihood-ratio estimation clearer. The calibration-probability correction, expanded proofs, and Appendix E improve checkability. These gains are limited by the largely retained central results, the lost simulation-learner description, and the newly incorrect L2-norm definition in Corollary 1.
